recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless THO changes or loses the CCN NamingSystem; future maintenance of this identifier belongs in THO/UTG rather than the FHIR core source checkout.
issue_request: FHIR-27035 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I R5 change request asking core to add a URL for the CMS Certification Number OID 2.16.840.1.113883.4.336 to the Identifier Registry. The accepted resolution was to add a URL for the OID and follow the pattern of working with CMS to get a URL assigned.
initial_application: No core git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-27035 was found. The application path is through terminology governance: the FHIR-27035 Jira comment says the request is now done at terminology.hl7.org/NamingSystem-CCN.html, HTA-48 approved the CCN identifier URI, and UP-253 implemented a THO NamingSystem named CCN. The core identifier-registry page was later changed by FHIR-35932 in git commit f40fc710c3 to remove the local identifier table after migration to HL7 Terminology.
additional_context: Current core source keeps identifier-registry.html in the build and states that identifier systems are actively curated in HL7 Terminology, with THO-defined URIs taking precedence for R5 conformance. Current THO exposes NamingSystem/CCN with OID 2.16.840.1.113883.4.336 and preferred URI http://terminology.hl7.org/NamingSystem/CMSCertificationNumber. A later parallel core request, FHIR-27898, was resolved Not Persuasive/No Change because the agreed URL belonged under THO rather than FHIR-I; the matching Zulip thread records that R4 would not be revised and R5 would point the identifier-registry page to THO.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Re-adding a local core registry row for CCN would undo the FHIR-35932 migration model, while the current core page already directs implementers to the active THO registry that contains the requested CCN OID and URL.

related_jiras.note: A later same-request R4 tracker was resolved No Change because the agreed CCN URL already belonged in THO, not core.
Published core issue migrated the Identifier Registry table to HL7 Terminology, making THO the active registry for CCN.
Terminology authority work approved the CMS Certification Number identifier URI.
UTG/THO proposal implemented the CCN NamingSystem.
